title: ALDER BENCH — A spoon maker at work, 14 deliverables

# ALDER BENCH

## Story
- Feature title: A spoon, from blank to bowl
- Studio: ALDER BENCH
- Publication: studio craft journal and studio campaign channels
- Subject: Nora Ellis
- Occupation: wooden spoon maker
- Experience: 18 years
- Working material: cherrywood
- Subject participation: approved for this journal and studio campaign
- Session: 21 October 2026, 09:00–12:00
- Locations: 1 workshop

## Subject identity
- Age: 48
- Dominant hand: right
- Hair: chin-length straight gray bob, center part
- Eyes: brown
- Distinguishing feature: small mole on left cheek
- Shirt: indigo cotton, long sleeves rolled to the elbows
- Apron: rust canvas, one square chest pocket, waist ties
- Trousers: charcoal
- Footwear: brown lace-up boots
- Jewelry: none

## Tools and workpiece
| Item | Fixed characteristics |
| --- | --- |
| Straight carving knife | Pale ash handle; straight steel blade |
| Hook knife | Dark walnut handle; curved steel blade |
| Spoon | Cherrywood; oval bowl; tapered handle; rounded handle end |
| Finished spoon dimensions | Length 240 mm; maximum bowl width 65 mm |
| Grain landmark | Dark curved streak along the bowl's left rim, continuing toward the handle |
| Blank | Rough spoon outline; solid bowl area; visible tool facets |
| Hollowing | Same outline and grain landmark; partially excavated bowl |
| Oiled | Completed bowl; smoothed handle; warm satin surface |

## Workshop geometry
- Coordinate origin: northwest interior corner
- Coordinate axes: x eastward, y southward
- Room: 6000 × 4000 mm
- North window: x 1600–4000 mm on north wall; center height 1400 mm above floor
- Bench: x 1800–4200 mm; y 1200–2100 mm; height 850 mm
- Tool cabinet: x 5200–5800 mm; y 800–2300 mm; height 1800 mm
- Door opening: west wall, y 3000–3900 mm
- Working position: x 3000 mm; y 900 mm
- C1: x 3000 mm; y 3200 mm
- C2: x 1000 mm; y 3000 mm
- C3: x 4800 mm; y 3200 mm
- South camera clearance: 900 mm from bench edge
- Workshop mark: square dark walnut plaque, three equal vertical recessed slots, above east-wall cabinet
- Walls: warm gray plaster, #D8D2C8
- Floor: matte gray concrete

## Light
- Main light: north window
- Modifier: white reflector
- Lit-side-to-shadow-side ratio: 2:1
- White balance: 5200 K
- Surface character: visible skin texture, wood fibers and tool wear

## Publication geometry and copy
- Spread trim: 360 × 240 mm
- Spread bleed: 3 mm on each outer edge
- Spread fold: 180 mm from left trim edge
- Portrait crop: central 160 × 240 mm area of the spread image; 2:3
- Square detail treatment: 1:1
- Face, hands and spoon clearance from fold: at least 12 mm
- Face, hands, spoon and printed-copy inset from relevant trim or crop edges: at least 9 mm
- Opening portrait copy: ALDER BENCH
- Opening portrait feature title: A spoon, from blank to bowl
- Film end-card and presentation-cover copy: ALDER BENCH; A spoon, from blank to bowl
- Film duration: 10 seconds
- Film sequence: Blank; Hollowing; Oiled

steps.userMessage:
ALDER BENCH | A spoon maker at work

We are commissioning an environmental portrait story about Nora Ellis, the spoon maker behind ALDER BENCH, for our craft journal and studio channels. Nora is our approved subject: 48 years old, right-handed, with a chin-length straight gray bob, brown eyes and a small mole on her left cheek. Her clothing throughout is an indigo cotton shirt, a rust canvas apron with one square chest pocket, charcoal trousers and brown lace-up boots. The attached identity sheet fixes her appearance. Follow her working sequence from a rough cherrywood blank through hollowing to an oiled spoon, 240 mm long with a 65 mm-wide oval bowl. The tools are a straight carving knife with a pale ash handle and a hook knife with a dark walnut handle.

The documentary direction is already set: working gestures, visible wood fibers and a readable relationship between Nora, her tools and her bench. Work takes place in one session, 09:00–12:00 on 21 October 2026, inside the 6000 × 4000 mm workshop. The north window is the main light; its center is 1400 mm above the floor. Use a white reflector for a 2:1 lit-side-to-shadow-side ratio and a 5200 K white balance. The plaster walls are warm gray #D8D2C8. Preserve the bench, east-wall tool cabinet and existing three-slot workshop mark in their mapped positions. Maintain the 900 mm camera clearance south of the bench. The opening portrait serves a 360 × 240 mm magazine spread with 3 mm bleed and a portrait social crop; detail D03 supplies the square treatment. Print "ALDER BENCH" and "A spoon, from blank to bowl" on both opening portrait treatments, and on the film end card and presentation cover where those deliverables apply.

Audience: readers of cultural magazines and craft brands, with the journal editor and studio owner selecting the story for publication and the studio campaign.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md records Nora's background, wardrobe, materials, lighting and publication facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable's proportion, format and stage. 03-shot-records.en.md records the shot IDs, subjects, camera stations and narrative order. workshop-plan.png fixes the room geometry, window, furniture, camera stations and clearance. publication-crops.png records the spread, portrait crop, square treatment and protected areas. nora-identity.png establishes Nora's front and profile appearance and complete wardrobe. spoon-and-tools.png establishes the two knives and the spoon at three stages. workshop-mark.png establishes the existing three-slot mark. empty-workshop-light.png supplies the empty room's window-light atmosphere.

Deliverables:
1. One two-page photographic language and lighting specification, stating the north-window position, 2:1 light ratio, white reflector, 5200 K white balance, selected shutter and aperture settings, and a shot register for the eleven still-image outputs
2. Four portrait photographs: opening spread P01, same-exposure portrait crop P01-V, seated working portrait P02 and standing inspection portrait P03
3. Three environment photographs: E01 linking Nora, window, bench and cabinet; E02 looking across the bench toward the cabinet; E03 showing Nora returning the tools
4. Four craft detail photographs: D01 rough blank and straight knife, D02 right-handed hollowing, D03 square finished-spoon view and D04 the hook blade meeting the bowl, each with its shot ID and stage caption
5. One 10-second studio film following Blank, Hollowing and Oiled in that order, with Nora, the two knives, the same spoon and a closing title card
6. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the specification, all eleven still-image outputs and three film frames, with the story ordered from arrival at the bench to the completed spoon

Acceptance:
- The specification precedes the photographs and sets out all eleven shot IDs, proportions and camera stations. Its north-window position, 2:1 ratio and 5200 K setting recur on presentation page 2; each reproduced photograph in the presentation carries its matching shot ID and proportion.
- All four portraits, all three environment photographs and the film preserve Nora's identity-sheet appearance and wardrobe. D02, D04 and the film's hollowing passage show the walnut-handled hook knife operated in her right hand; the straight knife retains its pale ash handle wherever it appears.
- P01 and P01-V share one exposure and print ALDER BENCH and A spoon, from blank to bowl; the film end card and presentation cover repeat both strings. The two portraits retain Nora's face, both hands and the entire spoon within the crop protections: 12 mm from the spread fold and 9 mm inside trim or crop boundaries.
- E01–E03 follow the workshop plan, their recorded camera stations and the 900 mm clearance; the east-wall mark retains its three slots. The portraits, environments, details and film follow the specification's north-window direction, 2:1 ratio and 5200 K setting.
- D01–D04 carry the stage captions in 03-shot-records.en.md and retain the three-stage sheet's cherrywood grain and evolving outline. D03 shows the finished 240 mm spoon and 65 mm-wide bowl; the film presents Blank, Hollowing and Oiled in sequence across its 10 seconds.
- The presentation contains at least eight pages, reproduces all eleven still-image outputs and three film frames, and identifies the images showing right-handed work, the two knife handles and the finished spoon dimensions.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
